sections.section_title: The Greeting -- Truth, Love, and the Indwelling Reality
sections.summary: The elder greets the elect lady (a church community) and her children, establishing truth and love as the twin foundations of the relationship, with truth abiding in them forever, and declaring that grace, mercy, and peace will be with them from God the Father and Jesus Christ the Son of the Father.

sections.section_title: The Elder's Joy -- Finding Children Walking in Truth
sections.summary: The elder rejoices at finding some of the community's members walking in truth, in accordance with the commandment received from the Father.

sections.section_title: The Commandment from the Beginning -- Love and Obedience as One
sections.summary: The elder restates the original commandment to love one another, defines love as walking according to God's commandments, and frames the commandment as what the community has had from the beginning -- creating a circular definition in which love and obedience are mutually defining.

sections.section_title: The Deceivers, the Antichrist, and the Danger of Departing from the Teaching
sections.summary: The neutral reading found that many deceivers have gone out who deny the incarnation, that the community must watch itself so as not to lose what has been worked for, and that everyone who goes beyond and does not abide in the teaching of Christ does not have God -- while the one who abides has both the Father and the Son.
sections.relevance: This passage directly addresses whether a believer's standing can be forfeited. Verse 8 warns: 'Watch yourselves, so that you do not lose what we have worked for, but that you may receive a full reward.' The neutral reading was emphatic: 'The warning presupposes that what has been gained is not automatically permanent. It can be lost. The deceivers pose a real threat to something the community actually possesses.' The verb apolesete ('you lose') describes destruction of something already possessed. Verse 9 establishes an absolute binary: 'Everyone who goes ahead and does not abide in the teaching of Christ does not have God.' The elder warns that advancing beyond the received teaching about the Christ results in losing God. The neutral reading stated: 'There is no middle ground. The teaching of the Christ is the line, and one stands on one side or the other.' The passage presents the community's present standing as genuinely at risk from false teaching, and frames the loss as real and consequential -- not merely hypothetical.
key_phrases: watch yourselves, so that you do not lose what we have worked for
but that you may receive a full reward
everyone who goes ahead and does not abide in the teaching of Christ does not have God
the one who abides in the teaching, this one has both the Father and the Son

sections.section_title: The Prohibition of Hospitality -- Practical Response to the Deceivers
sections.summary: The elder instructs the community not to receive into the house or greet anyone who does not bring the teaching of Christ, because extending fellowship to a false teacher creates participation in his evil works.

sections.section_title: The Closing -- Anticipated Visit and Greetings
sections.summary: The elder expresses his preference for face-to-face communication over writing, anticipates a visit so that their joy may be made complete, and relays greetings from the children of the elect sister community.
